numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When called with exactly two data points, `stats.linregress` returns `pvalue=0.0`, `stderr=0.0`, and `intercept_stderr=0.0` instead of NaN/infinite/otherwise non-finite inferential quantities for the degenerate case (0 residual degrees of freedom).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For exactly two points, the discussion notes that `pvalue`, `stderr`, and `intercept_stderr` should not be treated as having zero uncertainty; specifically, returning `NaN` for `pvalue`, `stderr`, and `intercept_stderr` is described as the fix, and returning `NaN` for all three is considered appropriate (alternatively some argue infinite standard errors).
trigger_conditions: Input contains exactly two data points (n == 2)
Execution reaches the n==2 degenerate/zero residual degrees of freedom case

input_output_examples.buggy_output: LinregressResult(slope=np.float64(1.0), intercept=np.float64(0.0), rvalue=np.float64(1.0), pvalue=0.0, stderr=0.0, intercept_stderr=0.0)
input_output_examples.source: issue#24684 reproducer output shows pvalue=0.0, stderr=0.0, intercept_stderr=0.0; PR description says to return NaN for pvalue/stderr/intercept_stderr when input contains exactly two points

oracle_clues: The issue states that for the special case of two data points, results that would produce NaNs are replaced with `pvalue=0.0`, `stderr=0.0`, and `intercept_stderr=0.0`.
The stated fix PR description: update `stats.linregress` to return `NaN` for `pvalue`, `stderr` and `intercept_stderr` when input contains exactly two points.

category_specific_evidence: Violated mathematical/degenerate-estimation property: with exactly n=2 points there are zero residual degrees of freedom (df = n - 2 = 0), so residual variance is undefined; therefore inferential quantities depending on residual variance/standard errors should be NaN rather than 0.0.

PR body states: “return `NaN` for `pvalue`, `stderr` and `intercept_stderr` when the input contains exactly two points… with only two data points, there are zero residual degrees of freedom, making the estimation of residual variance undefined.”

Example outputs from issue reproducer (exactly two points): stats.linregress([0, 1], [0, 1]) gives slope=1.0, intercept=0.0, rvalue=1.0, pvalue=0.0, stderr=0.0, intercept_stderr=0.0 (these are the concrete values demonstrating the incorrect/changed behavior in the n=2 degenerate case).

Test change shows the expected numerical behavior for the two-point degenerate case: it now sets NaN = xp.asarray(xp.nan) and asserts rvalue, pvalue, stderr, intercept_stderr are NaN (xp_assert_equal(result.rvalue, NaN), xp_assert_equal(result.pvalue, NaN), xp_assert_equal(result.stderr, NaN), xp_assert_equal(result.intercept_stderr, NaN)).

R output in the issue shows the same degenerate degrees-of-freedom concept: “ALL 2 residuals are 0: no residual degrees of freedom!” and “Residual standard error: NaN on 0 degrees of freedom”, with NaNs for coefficient standard errors and t/p values (Intercept and x show Std. Error = NaN, t value = NaN, Pr(>|t|) = NaN).
reproduction_risks: Input must have exactly two points (n=2) to trigger the zero residual degrees-of-freedom / undefined residual variance regime.

Behavior may vary by backend/array API handling (mentions of dtype preservation and nan_scalar handling), so reproduction should use the same numerical backend expectations as in the referenced tests/issues.

When n=2 and residual variance is undefined, additional outputs (rvalue, pvalue, stderr, intercept_stderr) are the key fields expected to become NaN per the test/PR description; comparing only slope/intercept could miss the failure mode.
